searchText: Where in the go-ethereum codebase does the ExcessBlobGas for a header goes from nil to non-nil during Cancun hardfork? I haven't found it in the codebase. Because the parent will have nil value but the current block after Cancun will have non-nil value. what block is dencun live on holesky? https://blog.ethereum.org/2024/01/24/sepolia-holesky-dencun ty can you submit a partially filled blob as a rollup? Or do you need to pad it with zeros. I don't understand the rationale to not allow partial blobs Why do you say that? https://sepolia.blobscan.com/block/5232971 How does blobscan get the gas price? https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/bc0b87ca196f92e5af49bd33cc190ef0ec32b197/miner/worker.go#L953-L958 first block is calculated with `(0, 0)` headers from outside will be verified It's derived from excess blob gas which is on chain you need to pad it with zeros if you want to post data under the blob size, is there an issue with padding with zeros? You pay for it don't you? Nonzero calldata has the same price as zero calldata. Just not sure on the rational and looking for motivation to understand the design choice It's not so much padded with zeros as encoded as a polynomial. Blobs aren't just a simple byte array that's passed around, they're 4096 field elements in something something mathy whatnot thing (Dankrad tried to explain the full math to me twice but it was my 5am so...). There are two big advantages for this, firstly it sets the groundwork for data availability sampling that's planned for full danksharding which reduces networking requirements and improves reliability. Secondly, it allows a small part of a blob to be loaded and proven. If you use a simple keccak or sha256 hash to verify the data you have to post it all, but with the kzg commitments used you can post a proof of just the smaller slice of data. This is a big advantage for things like fault proof systems which in a dispute may need to access some of the actual blob data in the EVM (and thus post it as calldata during hte dispute process). Ah ok so it's a math reason Edit https://dankradfeist.de/ethereum/2022/03/16/exponential-eip1559.html
